title: AI Agents
lede: Where a workflow ends and an agent begins. A few questions on tools, memory, loops and the failure modes nobody warns you about.
description: Where a workflow ends and an agent begins. Test what you know about tools, memory, loops and the failure modes nobody warns you about.

questions.q: What most clearly separates an AI agent from a workflow?
options: The agent uses a bigger model
The agent decides its own next step; a workflow follows a path you fixed in advance
The agent runs in the cloud
The agent costs more to run
questions.why: Control flow is the dividing line. If you decided the sequence up front, it's a workflow — however clever the steps are.

questions.q: An agent keeps repeating the same failing tool call. What's the most likely cause?
options: The model is too small
It can't see the result of its own action clearly enough to change course
The internet connection is slow
Too many tools are connected
questions.why: Loops usually come from weak feedback. If the tool result doesn't clearly say what went wrong, the agent has no reason to try something different.

questions.q: When is a plain workflow the better choice over an agent?
options: When the steps are known, repeatable and must work the same way every time
Whenever the task involves text
When you have a small budget
When you don't have coding skills
questions.why: Predictable work deserves a predictable system. Save agents for tasks where the path genuinely varies.

questions.q: An agent needs to remember what happened in earlier steps of a long task. What usually helps most?
options: A bigger context window alone
A structured memory or state the agent can read and update between steps
Asking the user to repeat context each time
Running the same prompt twice
questions.why: Long tasks need explicit state. Raw context fills up; a scratchpad or memory object gives the agent something stable to build on.

questions.q: You're connecting five tools to an agent. What's the main risk?
options: The UI gets cluttered
The model may pick the wrong tool or chain calls in a fragile order
Tools always slow the model down
You need five API keys
questions.why: More tools mean more ways to mis-route. Clear descriptions, fewer tools where possible, and guardrails on when each runs reduce failure.
